name: S3FileContent
title: S3 File Content
description: Read one S3 object's details, mint a link to fetch it, and optionally read its text
whenToUse: Pick when you have a specific object and need a way to get at it: its size and type, plus a time-limited link a later step can fetch without AWS credentials. Switched on, it also reads the object's body as text, so a stored markdown or CSV file lands straight in the next step. Finding out what is in a bucket is a different job.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: The file to read, as { key } or a whole file object from S3 Files. Its bucket, size and id are carried through when present.

outputs.name: file
outputs.description: key, bucket, size, contentType, lastModified, etag, universalId, downloadUrl, and content (the body as text, when Include Content is on)

bucket.title: S3 Bucket
bucket.description: The bucket the object lives in

key.title: Key
key.description: The object's key. Leave empty to take it from the incoming signal.

includeContent.title: Include Content
includeContent.description: Also fetch the object's body and return it as `content`, read as text. For a markdown, CSV or JSON object this hands the words straight to the next step with no second fetch. Leave off for binary or very large objects; the link is the way to move those.

downloadUrlExpiry.title: Link Lifetime (seconds)
downloadUrlExpiry.description: How long the download link stays valid. The retired node always used seven days, which is the maximum AWS allows; a day is usually plenty.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: aws-s3
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# S3 AS MANIFESTS. The same signer as DynamoDB, plus the three things S3 needs that a plain
# JSON API does not:
#
#   transport: xml     S3's list endpoints never moved to JSON
#   transport: headers a HEAD reply IS its headers, which is how size and type arrive
#   presign            links that carry their own authority, so something with no credentials
#                      can fetch the object
#
# COMPLETE as of 2026-07-27. An earlier note here said S3Upload could not be a manifest
# because a binary request BODY was missing. That was true when it was written and is not
# now: `encoding: binary` sends bytes rather than JSON, so S3Upload is the third node here.
#
# The note was also wrong about the consequence. It said S3Upload "stays TypeScript until
# then", but the TypeScript had already gone to `_legacy/` with the rest of the package, so
# the node type did not exist at all and any saved workflow using it was broken. Retiring a
# package is all-or-nothing, and a per-node exception in prose does not create one.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/aws-s3/`.

name: aws-s3
displayName: AWS S3
description: List, read and write objects in AWS S3, with shareable links
version: 2.1.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749916163/gravity/icons/Amazon-S3-Logo.svg.png

features:
  - List a bucket or prefix, filtered by extension
  - Read one object's metadata
  - Write a file from a url or base64
  - Presigned links, so a downstream step needs no credentials

allowedHosts:
  - "**.amazonaws.com"
  # Any host, for the UNAUTHENTICATED source fetch in S3Upload only. It pulls the file from a
  # url a person supplies, which cannot be declared in advance. That call sends no credential,
  # and the executor refuses "*" the moment one does. Non-https is refused regardless.
  - "*"

requires:
  credential: [awsSigV4]
  transport: [xml, headers, binary, text]
  # NOTE: `encoding: binary`, which the PUT in S3Upload depends on, has no field in `requires`
  # to declare it, so it is gated only by executorVersion below. Same gap `aws-dynamodb` has
  # with `dynamodbJson`.
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.awsCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# Transcribed from plugin-base's shared AWSCredential, NAME AND FIELDS UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `awsCredential` keep resolving. Every AWS package
# shares this one, exactly as they shared the TypeScript definition.
#
# sessionToken is NEW, and additive. The retired definition had no such field, so anyone on
# temporary credentials (an assumed role, anything via STS) could not use these nodes at
# all. The signer sends and signs it only when it is filled in.

name: awsCredential
displayName: AWS Credentials
description: AWS credentials for AWS services (DynamoDB, S3, Bedrock, and the rest)
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html

properties:
  - name: accessKeyId
    displayName: Access Key ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Access Key ID
    placeholder: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
  - name: secretAccessKey
    displayName: Secret Access Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Secret Access Key
    placeholder: ""
  - name: region
    displayName: AWS Region
    type: string
    required: false
    default: us-east-1
    description: The region your tables live in
    placeholder: us-east-1
  - name: sessionToken
    displayName: Session Token
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: Only for temporary credentials from STS or an assumed role. Leave empty for a long-lived key.
    placeholder: ""

shared.files.yaml:
# THE FILTERED FILE LIST, derived once and shared by everything that needs it.
#
# Two places need the same list in the SAME ORDER: the presign entry mints a link per key,
# and the output pairs each link back to its file by index. Deriving it twice would be two
# expressions free to drift, and a drift here attaches the wrong link to a file — an error
# that looks exactly like an answer.
#
# WHAT THE FILTERS ARE FOR. S3 has no real directories: a folder made in the console is a
# zero-byte object whose key ends in "/", and a later ingest step would try to fetch it as a
# document. Both filters are transcribed from the retired node for that reason.

objects: &objects >-
  return ((((calls.list || {}).ListBucketResult || {}).Contents) || [])
    .filter(o => o.Key && !String(o.Key).endsWith('/'))
    .filter(o => !(Number(o.Size) === 0 && String(o.Key).includes('/')))
    .filter(o => !(config.fileExtensions || []).length
      || (config.fileExtensions || []).map(e => String(e).toLowerCase())
           .includes(String(o.Key).split('.').at(-1).toLowerCase()))

# Just the keys, for `presign.for`. Same filters, same order.
keys: &keys >-
  return ((((calls.list || {}).ListBucketResult || {}).Contents) || [])
    .filter(o => o.Key && !String(o.Key).endsWith('/'))
    .filter(o => !(Number(o.Size) === 0 && String(o.Key).includes('/')))
    .filter(o => !(config.fileExtensions || []).length
      || (config.fileExtensions || []).map(e => String(e).toLowerCase())
           .includes(String(o.Key).split('.').at(-1).toLowerCase()))
    .map(o => String(o.Key))

# The output shape, links folded in by index.
#
# universalId is transcribed exactly from the retired executor: sha256 of
# `key|size|lastModified`, first 12 chars. It includes SIZE AND DATE deliberately, so an
# object replaced at the same key gets a NEW id and is not mistaken for the old one. Copying
# the formula rather than inventing one keeps ids stable across the migration, which matters
# because other tables join on them.
files: &files >-
  return ((((calls.list || {}).ListBucketResult || {}).Contents) || [])
    .filter(o => o.Key && !String(o.Key).endsWith('/'))
    .filter(o => !(Number(o.Size) === 0 && String(o.Key).includes('/')))
    .filter(o => !(config.fileExtensions || []).length
      || (config.fileExtensions || []).map(e => String(e).toLowerCase())
           .includes(String(o.Key).split('.').at(-1).toLowerCase()))
    .map((o, i) => Object.assign({
      key: String(o.Key),
      size: Number(o.Size) || 0,
      lastModified: String(o.LastModified || ''),
      etag: String(o.ETag || '').split('"').join(''),
      bucket: config.bucket,
      universalId: sha256(String(o.Key) + '|' + (Number(o.Size) || 0) + '|' + String(o.LastModified || '')).substring(0, 12)
    }, (calls.links || [])[i] ? { presignedUrl: (calls.links || [])[i] } : {}))
shared.s3.yaml:
# What both nodes share.
#
# S3 addresses a bucket as a SUBDOMAIN (virtual-hosted style), which is the modern form and
# the one that keeps working as path-style is retired. It also puts the bucket name in the
# host, so allowedHosts covers it with one subdomain level.

call: &call
  credential:
    scheme: awsSigV4
    service: s3
  # S3 speaks XML on its list endpoints. Parsed to a plain object, so the events tables read
  # like every other node's.
  transport: xml
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [500, 502, 503, 504]

# The bucket's own host. Written once because getting it wrong is a SIGNATURE failure rather
# than a 404, and that is a much harder error to read back to its cause.
host: &host >-
  return config.bucket + '.s3.' + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1') + '.amazonaws.com'
shared.upload.yaml:
# WHAT IS BEING UPLOADED, derived here so the request and the output cannot disagree.
#
# The bytes go in the PUT body, the content type goes in its header, and both the type and the
# size go on the output. Deriving them where they are used would put copies in two files, and
# a drift between those copies uploads one thing while reporting another.
#
# `contentType` and the size appear twice WITHIN this file, because a $ref substitutes a whole
# YAML value and neither can be spliced into the middle of the output expression. Same reason
# `files.yaml` repeats its filter chain. Keeping the copies in one file is the point: a reader
# sees them together and can check they agree, which is not true of copies in separate files.
#
# WHY THE STRIPPING EXISTS. A base64 field is very often filled from something that produced a
# DATA URL, "data:image/png;base64,iVBOR...", because that is what a browser file read and most
# image APIs hand back. Uploading it verbatim writes that literal text into the object, which
# succeeds, reports a plausible size, and produces a file nothing can open. The retired node
# stripped the prefix for that reason and this keeps doing it.

# The bytes. On the url path this is `calls.source` WHOLE, because `encoding: binary` accepts
# either a base64 string or the { base64 } object the binary transport produced. On the base64
# path it is everything after the last comma, since base64 itself contains none. On the text
# path the text is encoded here (`toBase64`, UTF-8), because base64 is the only form bytes
# take on the way to `encoding: binary` — parsed markdown written back to S3 is the case.
payload: &payload >-
  return config.sourceType === 'url'
    ? (calls.source || {})
    : config.sourceType === 'text'
    ? toBase64(config.textData || '')
    : (String(config.base64Data || '').includes(',')
        ? String(config.base64Data || '').split(',').at(-1)
        : String(config.base64Data || ''))

# What the file IS. An explicit setting wins, then whatever the source declared: the url's own
# reply header, or the data URL's prefix between the colon and the semicolon. The fallback is
# the one S3 assumes anyway, stated rather than left implicit.
contentType: &contentType >-
  return config.contentType
    || (config.sourceType === 'url'
          ? ((calls.source || {}).contentType || '')
          : config.sourceType === 'text'
          ? 'text/markdown; charset=utf-8'
          : (String(config.base64Data || '').startsWith('data:')
              ? String(config.base64Data || '').slice(5).split(';')[0] : ''))
    || 'application/octet-stream'

# The output shape.
#
# `s3Url` is the object's own address and needs credentials to fetch. `downloadUrl` is the
# presigned one and does not. Both are returned because they answer different questions: where
# the file lives, and how to hand it to something with no AWS access. The retired node used
# these two names, so both keep them.
#
# The SIZE is only derived here, and it is not the base64 string length: base64 spends 4
# characters on every 3 bytes and pads the last group with '=', so the raw length would
# overstate every upload by a third. On the url path the binary transport already counted them.
# `s3Url` is the presigned link MINUS its query, not rebuilt from the credential's region:
# the output expression runs in the EMIT scope, which carries `calls` but no `credentials`
# (found live — the node wrote the object, then died emitting). The presign already encoded
# the same bucket/region/key, so stripping the query is the same address with no second
# derivation to drift.
output: &output >-
  return {
    key: String(config.key || ''),
    bucket: config.bucket,
    s3Url: (((calls.link || [])[0] || '').split('?')[0]),
    downloadUrl: (calls.link || [])[0] || '',
    size: config.sourceType === 'url'
      ? (Number((calls.source || {}).bytes) || 0)
      : config.sourceType === 'text'
      ? Math.max(0, Math.floor(toBase64(config.textData || '').length / 4 * 3)
          - (toBase64(config.textData || '').endsWith('==') ? 2
             : toBase64(config.textData || '').endsWith('=') ? 1 : 0))
      : Math.max(0, Math.floor(
          (String(config.base64Data || '').includes(',')
            ? String(config.base64Data || '').split(',').at(-1)
            : String(config.base64Data || '')).length / 4 * 3)
          - (String(config.base64Data || '').endsWith('==') ? 2
             : String(config.base64Data || '').endsWith('=') ? 1 : 0)),
    contentType: config.contentType
      || (config.sourceType === 'url'
            ? ((calls.source || {}).contentType || '')
            : config.sourceType === 'text'
            ? 'text/markdown; charset=utf-8'
            : (String(config.base64Data || '').startsWith('data:')
                ? String(config.base64Data || '').slice(5).split(';')[0] : ''))
      || 'application/octet-stream'
  }

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector.
#
# Everything comes from the HEAD's headers plus what the incoming signal already knew. The
# retired node got `size` by downloading the entire object and measuring it, then threw the
# bytes away; content-length says the same thing without moving the file.
#
# The signal's own fields are carried through where S3 cannot supply them: a universalId
# minted by S3 Files upstream is the join key other tables use, so losing it here would
# break the link between this file and everything already recorded about it.

# `calls.head`, NOT `response`: the LAST call here is the presign, so `response` is the minted
# url list — the headers live under the head call's own name. Reading them off `response` was
# authored before this node ever ran end-to-end (the presign-as-final-call path only started
# working 2026-08-05) and produced a file whose size, type and dates were all silently empty.
- emit: file
  from: response
  value: >-
    return {
      key: String(config.key || signal.key || ''),
      bucket: config.bucket,
      size: Number((calls.head || {})['content-length']) || 0,
      contentType: (calls.head || {})['content-type'] || 'application/octet-stream',
      lastModified: (calls.head || {})['last-modified'] || signal.lastModified || '',
      etag: String((calls.head || {}).etag || signal.etag || '').split('"').join(''),
      universalId: signal.universalId || sha256(config.bucket + '/' + String(config.key || signal.key || '')).substring(0, 12),
      downloadUrl: (calls.link || [])[0] || '',
      content: String(calls.body || '')
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# HEAD for the metadata, then mint the link. Neither moves the file.

- $ref: s3#call
  name: head
  method: HEAD
  url: >-
    return 'https://' + config.bucket + '.s3.'
      + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1') + '.amazonaws.com/'
      + String(config.key || signal.key || '').split('/').map(s => encodeURIComponent(s)).join('/')
  # A HEAD has no body by definition: the size, type and modified date come back as HEADERS
  # and nothing else does. `transport: headers` is what makes them reachable.
  transport: headers

# The body itself, only when asked for. Read as TEXT: this is the lane for reaching into a
# stored markdown/CSV/JSON object, not for moving binaries — those travel by the link.
- $ref: s3#call
  name: body
  when: "return !!config.includeContent"
  method: GET
  url: >-
    return 'https://' + config.bucket + '.s3.'
      + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1') + '.amazonaws.com/'
      + String(config.key || signal.key || '').split('/').map(s => encodeURIComponent(s)).join('/')
  transport: text

- name: link
  presign:
    for: "return [String(config.key || signal.key || '')]"
    url: >-
      return 'https://' + config.bucket + '.s3.'
        + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1') + '.amazonaws.com/'
        + item.split('/').map(s => encodeURIComponent(s)).join('/')
    expiresIn: "return config.downloadUrlExpiry || 86400"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [bucket]
  properties:
    bucket:
      type: string
      title: S3 Bucket
      description: The bucket the object lives in
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    key:
      type: string
      title: Key
      description: The object's key. Leave empty to take it from the incoming signal.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    includeContent:
      type: boolean
      title: Include Content
      description: >-
        Also fetch the object's body and return it as `content`, read as text. For a
        markdown, CSV or JSON object this hands the words straight to the next step with
        no second fetch. Leave off for binary or very large objects; the link is the way
        to move those.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    downloadUrlExpiry:
      type: number
      title: Link Lifetime (seconds)
      description: >-
        How long the download link stays valid. The retired node always used seven days,
        which is the maximum AWS allows; a day is usually plenty.
      default: 86400
      minimum: 60
      maximum: 604800
"ui:order": [bucket, key, includeContent, downloadUrlExpiry]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: >-
      The file to read, as { key } or a whole file object from S3 Files. Its bucket, size
      and id are carried through when present.
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: file
    type: object
    description: >-
      key, bucket, size, contentType, lastModified, etag, universalId, downloadUrl, and
      content (the body as text, when Include Content is on)

credentials:
  - name: awsCredential
    required: true
    displayName: AWS
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: S3FileContent
kind: PromiseNode

name: S3 File Content
category: Storage & Data
color: "#FF9900"

description: Read one S3 object's details, mint a link to fetch it, and optionally read its text

whenToUse: >-
  Pick when you have a specific object and need a way to get at it: its size and type, plus
  a time-limited link a later step can fetch without AWS credentials. Switched on, it also
  reads the object's body as text, so a stored markdown or CSV file lands straight in the
  next step. Finding out what is in a bucket is a different job.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

# NOT AT PARITY, and the difference is deliberate. The retired node DOWNLOADED the whole
# object into memory to report its size, then discarded the bytes because passing them on
# "caused subscription issues". This asks S3 for the metadata instead (a HEAD), which
# returns the same size and content type without moving the file at all. For a large object
# that is the difference between a few hundred bytes and the whole thing.

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: the link carries an expiry, so a reused output hands back a dying link.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# NEEDS A REAL BUCKET AND KEY.

testData:
  config:
    bucket: REPLACE_WITH_A_REAL_BUCKET
    key: REPLACE_WITH_A_REAL_KEY
    downloadUrlExpiry: 86400
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    file: >-
      return output.file.size > 0
        && typeof output.file.contentType === 'string'
        && output.file.downloadUrl.includes('X-Amz-Signature=')
        && output.file.universalId.length === 12
